digest: HEAD 654f639 is not safe to ship as-is. The public terminal summary field was renamed from launchRetryAttempts to launchRetries, which SPEC T3 names as a public contract, with no alias. Cancellation and stop-detection behavior also changed in ways SPEC.md forbids or does not describe.

impacts.note: Breaking public field rename: WorkflowTerminalSummary.launchRetryAttempts is now launchRetries (src/workflow-terminal.ts:33,107). SPEC T3 names launchRetryAttempts as a public contract read by external tools. No alias or migration note exists, and no in-repo consumer was found.

Widened cancellation classification: src/workflow-cancellation.ts:16-20 adds 'cancelled' and 'timeout' string tokens and cancelled flags. SPEC C1 allows only aborted/AbortError/ABORT_ERR. Provider results that carry these words may now be treated as cancellation, which changes retry and semantic-status outcomes for consumers.

Stop detection by message: isWorkflowStopRequestedError also matches a message prefix. SPEC S6 forbids message matching, so errors whose message starts with 'workflow stop requested' may be misclassified.

Stop poll default changed: createWorkflowStopSignal uses pollMs ?? 200 (src/workflow-stop.ts:67), while SPEC S3 says 50ms with a 10ms floor. Code uses a 1ms floor. Stop-request latency rises up to about 200ms, and callers passing small values see different clamping.
Contract documentation drift: SPEC.md (S3, S6, C1, T3) is unchanged in HEAD and no longer describes the code. Consumers and reviewers relying on the spec will get wrong expectations.
No tests exist in the repo (package.json has only typecheck), so none of these changed behaviors is covered by a regression check.

assumptions.note: The HEAD diff could not be read directly; the change set was inferred from the commit message, the upstream artifacts, and grep confirmation of current code (launchRetries, pollMs default 200, 'cancelled'/'timeout' tokens).
No external consumers of launchRetries or launchRetryAttempts were found in this repo; their existence and count are unknown.
store.js and types.js are absent, so runtime behavior of the disk stop-intent path was not verified.
Intent behind the renames and widened matching (for example, whether 200ms was deliberate) is unknown.
